summary: MarketBeat host interviews Oxford Club guest Mark Lichtenfeld about finding genuinely cheap stocks instead of chasing the Nvidia dip, after Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO. Lichtenfeld says Nvidia is down about 30% from its highs and trades at roughly 17 times 2027 projected earnings, with its long-term story largely intact, but he advises waiting to see where the stock settles — hence NVDA UNCERTAIN (wait and see). His framework is fundamentals first, valuation second, charts third: buy when the business is solid and growing, the valuation is low, and the chart shows support or a breakout. His first pick is Ashland (ASH) BUY at $76: an ingredients maker, expected to grow earnings 28% in fiscal 2027 and 32% over the next two years at 18 times earnings, with activists adding two board members and pushing strategic alternatives; a comparable sale multiple implies $118, and 11% of the float sold short could fuel a squeeze. Second is Central Garden & Pet (CENTA) CONDITIONAL_BUY above a $45 breakout: a $2.6 billion recession-resistant pet and garden company at 14 times forward earnings, generating $300 million of free cash flow, sideways for five years, which he says could reach $60 if it breaks out. Third is HCA Healthcare (HCA) BUY: the largest US hospital network, at 17 times earnings versus a sector median of 20, with earnings projected to more than triple over ten years, strong Texas and Florida demographics, and political tailwinds from possible Medicaid-cut rollbacks.
